summary: The study describes the atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) of gallium arsenide (GaAs) using alternating pulses of Ga(CH3)3, AsH3, and atomic hydrogen. The process is carried out at temperatures between 430 and 500 “C to prevent thermal decomposition of Ga(CH3)3 while maintaining sufficient surface kinetics for growth. The use of atomic hydrogen pulses enhances the decomposition of adsorbed Ga(CH3)3 and AsH3 molecules, enabling monolayer-by-monolayer growth of GaAs. The growth is self-limiting, with a monolayer per cycle, and the process is demonstrated to be effective at lower temperatures than previously reported.
evidence: Monolayer atomic layer epitaxy of GaAs has been achieved between 430 and 500 “C by using alternating pulses of ASH3, Ga(CH3)3, and atomic hydrogen. Maintaining the susceptor temperature below 500 “C suppresses the unfavorable thermal decomposition of Ga(CH3)3 to Ga in the gas phase. The basic point of our growth method is that, notwithstanding these low temperatures, sufficiently fast surface kinetics for growth are maintained by activation with the atomic hydrogen pulses.
